correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the claimed finite certificate from the seven assigned frozen Git blobs (tree SHA exactly matched). For s=847/1000 and g(x)=1+(127/120)x, K_s^(12)g(x)-g(x) is the sum for a=1..12 of 4^(-a)[(a+x)^(1.694)+(127/120)(a+x)^(0.694)] minus 1-(127/120)x. Both exponents are positive, so on each cell [j/N,(j+1)/N] each positive summand is bounded below by its value at left endpoint while the subtracted linear g is bounded above at right endpoint. Independently performed this 60-digit mpmath.iv outward-enclosed endpoint proof for all N=2000 cells: worst lower endpoint >0.000051512874938653, attained at j=1005, exceeds 1/25000=0.00004; an independent N=4000 run also passed. This is an exhaustive finite interval proof of the CONTINUUM inequality, not samples; it differs from the source verifier which propagates intervals through the whole expression. Since every a>=13 summand is positive, full K_s g > g+1/25000. With g(x)<=247/120 it gives K_s g >= (1+3/154375)g. Iterating positivity and bounding operator norm gives r(K_s)>=1+3/154375>1. The directly inspected source Proposition 1 supplies strictly increasing P(s)=log r(K_s), unique zero D_2, so D_2<0.847. The source Fourier comparison eta_*<=D_2/2 yields eta_*<0.4235. No conclusion from a merely truncated finite numerical sum is used.
